title: 📉 'Nvidia' Shares Plunge 13% in One Day — an Investigation into Its Accounts Shakes Wall Street!
body: 📉 'Nvidia' Shares Plunge 13% in One Day — an Investigation into Its Accounts Shakes Wall Street!

"Nvidia" shares plunged about 13% on Friday, November 20, reaching about $127 after touching a 52-week low of $126.64, and its market value fell to about $3.05 trillion. The drop came after a report that US Securities and Exchange Commission enforcement staff are examining possible accounting practices at the company, without it yet being clear when the investigation began or exactly what it is examining.

A major financial newspaper had revealed on Tuesday that the agency is investigating the company, including whether its disclosures misled investors, and the new report added that the focus includes possible accounting issues. The agency declined to comment, and the company did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Scrutiny renewed over a change the company made last year in how it reports revenue by geographic region, moving from billing addresses to customer headquarters, so Singapore disappeared from the regional breakdown — while its sales there had approached half of global revenue.

The crisis comes after the resignation of the founder and former CEO on November 11, and the board's rejection of his offer to return, while the company searches for a permanent chief through an executive search firm. Although the company achieved record quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from the previous year, the decline wiped out more than a third of its market value, amid investor concern also about circular financing deals in which chipmakers help customers finance their purchases.

Simply put: the company leading the AI boom loses more than a third of its value in weeks, not because of its products, but because of questions about its accounts and leadership — trust in the market is worth more than the chips themselves.
Do you think the investigation will reveal real violations, or is it just temporary pressure on the stock?
